title: Budget and Revenue
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

Does having a bigger budgets result in a bigger box-office returns? Figure 1 plots each film’s budget against its Worldwide revenue. The values are in millions of US Dollars.

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (musd)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (musd)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Budget against Worldwide revenue

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

Do longer films get better rating? The Figure 1 plots each film’s runtime against its IMDb rating.

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (min)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Runtime against IMDb rating





Below you will be able to find the mean rating of each decade.

films["decade"] = films["year"] // 10 * 10
films.groupby("decade")["imdb_rating"].mean().round(2)

decade

title: Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")


bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

The following dataset will include the dataset of Bond films from 1995 to 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (musd)")
plt.show()
